title: Data Sciences, B.S. (Information Sciences and Technology)
notes: Built from the real archived 2024-25 bulletin edition (bulletins.psu.edu/archive/2024-2025/undergraduate/colleges/information-sciences-technology/data-sciences-bs/), cross-checked against its own archived Program Requirements PDF, verifying the Suggested Academic Plan table's printed semester subtotals (14/17/16/15/15/15/15/15 = Total Credits 123) against the raw HTML table cells directly. This is the first archive edition where the Third Year sequence matches 2026's live table -- DS 300/DS 305/DS 320/STAT 380 now in Fall, DS 310/DS 330/DS 410 now in Spring (confirmed directly in this edition's own raw HTML table; 2022 and 2023 both have the opposite order -- DS 310 in Fall, STAT 380 in Spring, per their own notes) -- so this file's Semester 5/6 sequence is swapped relative to DATSC-2022.json/DATSC-2023.json to match. Real bulletin-internal inconsistency found and documented rather than silently resolved: this edition's own HTML Suggested Academic Plan table already prints "DS 441" in the 8-option cross-listed elective group, but this SAME edition's own archived Program Requirements PDF still prints the pre-renumbering "IST 441" in its equivalent "Additional Courses" list (verified directly in both the raw HTML and the raw PDF text extraction -- not a WebFetch artifact). 2023's HTML and PDF agree with each other (both say IST 441); 2025's HTML and PDF agree with each other (both say DS 441); only 2024 has the two documents disagreeing with each other, meaning the renumbering took effect mid-cycle and one of the two 2024-25 documents wasn't updated to match. Both codes are kept as options in this file's two 8/9-option cross-listed-elective items (Semester 7 and 8), with DS 441/IST 445 kept as the scheduled default pick (matching the HTML plan, and consistent with 2025 being fully in sync on DS 441) and the PDF's contradicting IST 441 text flagged rather than silently dropped. Also newly named per-category headings appear on the bulletin page starting this edition (Astronomy, Business Fundamentals, Economics, Food Science, Human-Centered Design and Development, Information and Cybersecurity Sciences, Nutrition, Psychology) -- 2022/2023's tables carry no such headings and had to be content-matched by course set instead. Application Focus Selection real changes this edition (confirmed by direct content diff against 2023's and 2025's lists): Business Fundamentals gained FIN 100/301, MGMT 100/100W/301/301W, MKTG 221W/301/301W, and SCM 301 (all absent in 2022/2023); Economics lost ECON 404/406/408/421/424 (retired from the list, confirmed absent in both this edition's HTML and its own PDF, present in 2022/2023's); NUTR 175 was renamed NUTR 175N. The CYBER 221/451/454 and HCDD 311/331/411/412/413/IST 331/411/412/413 additions are NOT yet present this edition (confirmed absent in both HTML and PDF) -- those first appear in the 2025-26 edition (see DATSC-2025.json's notes); this file's regex omits them accordingly. BIOL/GEOSC 474 (Astrobiology) included in Astronomy per the PDF, as in every other year checked. MATH 21 added (Semester 3) for the same real, catalog-verified, non-year-versioned DS 200/STAT 184 prereq reason as every other year. STAT 184 still printed as 2 credits this edition (kept as printed, same as 2022/2023). All Program Requirements totals confirmed directly against this edition's own Program Requirements table 0. Also: this edition's own raw Suggested Academic Plan table has TWO "General Education Course" items in First Year Spring (row 4's Fall=GenEd/Spring=GenEd pairing plus row 5's Fall=PSU 17/Spring=GenEd pairing), summing to that semester's own printed 17-credit subtotal (MATH 141 4 + CMPSC 132 3 + DS 200 4 + GenEd 3 + GenEd 3 = 17) -- confirmed directly in the raw HTML table cells for this edition. DATSC-2026.json's own Semester 2 only lists ONE "GEN ED" slot (summing to 14, short of its own stated target_credits of "17") -- verified this is the same real gap in the live 2026-27 edition's own printed table, not specific to this year, so it's a pre-existing gap in the already-built 2026 file, out of scope for this file to fix. Added the second GEN ED slot here so this file's own Semester 2 matches this edition's own printed 17-credit subtotal exactly.
